Specialist practice

Visa operations management.Run to embassy standard.

Dagem leads visa application centres the way a consulate expects them to run: SOP-driven, continuity-ready, secure, measured through ERP data, and staffed by teams that know exactly what good looks like.

Centre operations & SLAs

Run the centre as a business unit: daily flow, service levels and profitability owned by one accountable leader.

  • Appointment, queue and slot capacity planned against forecast volumes
  • Shift rosters built for seasonal peaks, with cover for absence
  • Critical service levels tracked daily, with clear escalation paths
  • Revenue, productivity and value-added service targets reviewed weekly
  • Facilities and layout kept fit for purpose and mission-ready

SLA / CSLKPI trackingP&L ownership

SOPs & quality

Every process written down, version-controlled and followed, so quality does not depend on who is on shift.

  • Work-instruction manuals for each process, signed off before use
  • Change control: new processes briefed, tested and rolled out on plan
  • Internal process assessments and calibration of every team member
  • Audit and mystery-audit readiness all year round
  • Root-cause analysis and a closed action plan for each repeat error

SOP designISO-alignedRoot-cause analysis

Business continuity

A centre that keeps serving applicants and protecting passports when systems, power, people or premises fail.

  • Continuity plans for system outage, power loss, staffing shortfall and site closure
  • Manual fallback procedures so no applicant or passport is stranded
  • Backup, recovery and call-tree drills held on a schedule
  • Incidents logged and escalated inside a fixed time window
  • Post-incident review that ends in a tracked action plan

ISO 22301-alignedRecovery drillsIncident response

Operational ERP & data

The operating system behind the counter: workflows, controls and reporting that make performance visible.

  • ERP and application-management workflows configured around the SOP
  • Role-based access, audit trails and daily reconciliation
  • Productivity and conversion grids feeding live dashboards
  • Monthly operational reports to the mission, with actions tracked to closure
  • Data-quality checks that stop keying errors at the source

ERPDashboardsMonthly reports

Security & compliance

Physical and information security treated as a daily discipline, not an annual audit.

  • Access control and passport chain of custody from counter to dispatch
  • Applicant data protection and information-security controls
  • Cash handling and end-of-day reconciliation
  • Integrity and anti-bribery standards embedded in team conduct
  • Health, safety and environment compliance

ISO 27001-alignedAnti-briberyEHS

Mission & partner relations

Trusted, documented relationships with embassies and consulates, and with the partners around them.

  • Regular performance reviews with missions, with minuted actions
  • Fast, documented answers to mission queries and complaints
  • Document-scrutiny and biometrics quality held to mission rules
  • Travel agents, vendors and local partners managed to clear standards
  • New services and process changes agreed with the mission before rollout

Embassy-gradeMission SLAsPartner management

People & leadership

Teams led to consular standards: accurate, courteous and steady under peak pressure.

  • Supervisors, front-desk and biometrics teams led to a single standard
  • Manpower planning, onboarding and role-based training
  • Coaching, internal certifications and honest performance feedback
  • Attrition and absence risk managed early
  • A recognition culture that rewards accuracy and service

Team leadershipCoachingCertification

Where organizations get stuck.

Leadership has a credible ambition but no integrated system to turn it into accountable execution. Strategy, sales, customer insight, digital presence and technology run as separate workstreams.

  • Growth strategy

    Goals are not translated into prioritized initiatives, owners and operating metrics.

  • Pipeline visibility

    Stages, qualification rules and forecasting differ across teams and markets.

  • Market intelligence

    Customer evidence and competitor signals are fragmented or arrive too late.

  • AI adoption

    Use cases run as isolated experiments without value hypotheses, controls or owners.

  • Generative visibility

    Brand information is hard for search and AI answer systems to find, interpret and cite.

Phase 1 · Weeks 1–2

Discovery & baseline

Leadership interviews, review of goals, data, pipeline and channels, current-state map, agreed success measures.

Phase 2 · Weeks 3–4

Strategy & architecture

Prioritized use cases, target operating model, pipeline, data, intelligence and visibility design, approved backlog.

Phase 3 · Weeks 5–10

Build & activation

Agreed assets implemented, playbooks and dashboards built, selected workflows tested, users reviewed and trained.

Phase 4 · Weeks 11–12

Optimization & handover

Deliverables validated, gaps closed, documentation handed over, next-stage roadmap and owners agreed.

Governance is part of the build.

We distinguish completed activity from business outcomes, and we say plainly what the data can and cannot support.

  • Baseline before targets

    Success measures are agreed in discovery against your starting point. No revenue result is guaranteed.

  • Humans decide

    Human review boundaries, tested cases, and approval for consequential decisions and external communications.

  • Limits on the record

    Where data is incomplete, the limitation is documented, not dressed up as evidence.

  • Owners named

    Every system, metric, use case and workflow leaves with an accountable internal owner and a playbook.
